metadata.title: Volunteer
metadata.description: SAIN runs on volunteers. Six teams across Amsterdam, Utrecht and Groningen, three to ten hours a week, one short application reviewed as it arrives.

hero.heading: SAIN runs on volunteers
hero.intro: Every programme is free because people give a few hours a week to run it. This page is the work, what you get from it, and the way in.
hero.photoAlt: People working together at a table during a hackathon

work.heading: Six teams, three to ten hours a week
work.intro: Amsterdam, Utrecht and Groningen each run the same teams. Leads carry a team and report to the chapter’s director; team members carry a slice of it. Most roles are three to five hours a week, leads six to ten.

education.name: Education
education.description: Run course cohorts and discussion groups. Facilitate weekly sessions, support participants, and keep quality high across iterations.

events.name: Events
events.description: Plan and deliver the chapter's calendar. Hackathons, expert talks, socials, and the logistics behind them.

communications.name: Communications
communications.description: Writing, design, photography, video and the website. Make the chapter's work visible and on-brand.

community.name: Community
community.description: Welcome new members, be the first point of contact, and help people find their way into deeper involvement.

outreach.name: Outreach
outreach.description: Be SAIN's face on campus. Tabling, flyers, and inviting students to upcoming events.

researchOperations.name: Research operations
researchOperations.description: Keep the Project Hub running day to day. Onboard researchers and supervisors, track projects, and unblock problems.

work.paidStaff: SAIN also hires a small number of paid national staff when a role needs it. Those roles are listed with the open positions.

whatYouGet.heading: You leave with work you can point to
whatYouGet.intro: Volunteer roles at SAIN carry real ownership early. Leads report straight to chapter directors, and team members run cohorts, events and channels that actually happen. You work alongside people across Utrecht, Groningen and Amsterdam who are moving into the field themselves, and many of the introductions that matter later start here.
returns: Experience with real responsibility, not shadowing
A network across three chapter cities
A track record in the field: cohorts taught, events run, work published

quote.text: “Without this community I almost certainly wouldn’t be where I am.”
quote.project: Mapping research on AI alignment techniques and government interventions

howToApply.heading: One short application, reviewed as it arrives
howToApply.intro: All chapter applications go through the same short form: name, CV, and a one-page motivation letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so apply whenever you are ready.

apply.title: Apply.
apply.body: Pick the chapter and the role, attach your CV, and write a short motivation letter. One page is plenty.

hearBack.title: Hear back.
hearBack.body: We read applications as they arrive. First response within 2 to 3 weeks.

talk.title: Talk.
talk.body: A 30 to 45 minute call about the role, your motivation, and a small task or scenario relevant to the team.

start.title: Start.
start.body: If that goes well, onboarding begins with the next cycle, and joining at other dates is possible.

howToApply.noFit: No role that fits? Apply anyway. Tell us what you want to do in your motivation letter, and we will figure out together what works well for you.

foundChapter.heading: Want SAIN in your city?
foundChapter.intro: Founding a chapter is its own path, with its own playbooks and mentorship, and it lives with the community.

close.heading: Every free programme has volunteers behind it
close.body: A few hours a week, a team in your city, and applications reviewed on a rolling basis. The next cohort of courses, events and research support gets run by whoever joins now.
